title: Agentic AI
reading: The slide introduces the classical definition of an agent, pairing the standard Russell & Norvig agent-environment schematic with the textbook quotation defining an agent as anything that perceives its environment through sensors and acts on it through actuators. A closing line notes that this definition applies equally to embodied (physical robot) and digital (software) agents.

visuals.description: Rounded blue 'Agent' box on the left containing 'Sensors' at top, a '?' box in the middle, and 'Actuators' at bottom; arrows flow from the 'Environment' bar on the right into Sensors labelled 'Percepts', down through the '?' box, and out from Actuators back to the Environment labelled 'Actions'.
visuals.assertion: An agent forms a closed perception-action loop with its environment; the internal decision function (the '?') maps percepts to actions.

visuals.description: Quoted textbook definition attributed to Russell & Norvig, AI: A Modern Approach, with 'agent', 'environment', 'sensors', 'actuators' bolded.
visuals.assertion: An agent is anything that can be viewed as perceiving its environment through sensors and acting upon that environment through actuators.
